expected_title: Methodology and Tools for Reducing CubeSat Mission Failure
abstract: A CubeSat is considered a great engineering system used for space research in the last decade. This is dueto its simple design, low cost, and usage of open-source software and hardware tools. CubeSats are in highdemand for use in a multitude of ways. Universities invest in space studies by encouraging and educatingSTEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math) students to be involved in designing, implementing,and testing of CubeSats. Universities differ in their CubeSat missions. A 1U CubeSat can be launched intospace and operate on a simple mission for basic science experiments. CubeSats can also be deployed inclusters for space exploration. According to Swartwout, however, roughly 50% of CubeSats fail to fulfilltheir mission. Different reasons lead CubeSats to fail including power, mechanical, and communicationissues. Some researchers suggested for this high level of failure, that universities and research institutionsmainly focus on the system and component level design, while neglecting the elicitation of requirementsneeded beforehand. To minimize the rate of failure of CubeSat missions, this research proposes a frameworkfor CubeSat systems engineering. This system provides tools to help institutions with planning, collecting,elicitation, and documenting requirements in a well-defined manner. This paper focuses on universities’CubeSat projects designed by students and faculty members. Thus, a recent survey has been conducted bythe researcher to identify the challenges and needs of such groups. Plans for future work are also discussed.
